intended_object: For a nonzero velocity v ∈ ℂ, the "outward-first" ordered real basis (−i·v, v) of ℂ ≅ ℝ². This is the basis whose first vector is the outward normal (v turned clockwise by 90°) and whose second is the velocity, as in the outward-normal-first boundary orientation convention. Inferred from the docstring, the module documentation and the lemma `outwardFirstBasis_apply`.
explanation:
The definition takes the standard basis (1, i) of ℂ over ℝ and maps it by multiplication by the nonzero complex number −i·v, viewed as an ℝ-linear equivalence. The resulting vectors are −i·v and −i·v·i = v. This is exactly the pair (−i·v, v), as the companion lemma `outwardFirstBasis_apply` states.

The two vectors form a basis because −i·v ≠ 0, which the proof term `mul_ne_zero (neg_ne_zero.mpr I_ne_zero) hv` guarantees. Their determinant is |v|², which is positive, so the basis has the standard complex orientation (`orientation_outwardFirstBasis`).

The sign convention is right. For a positively oriented (counterclockwise) boundary the interior lies to the left, so the outward normal is v turned clockwise, which is −i·v. This also matches the flux identity in the same file, X dy − Y dx = ⟪(X, Y), −i·v⟫.

The object is a specific planar construction: it uses complex multiplication by −i to rotate. Working in ℂ is therefore part of what is being defined, not an unnecessary restriction. A broader version would be the basis (J·v, v) in an oriented 2-dimensional inner product space, but the docstring explicitly describes the complex-multiplication construction. Mathlib has no definition of this basis.
